# Feature: Coherent Deterministic Synthesis

## 1. Feature Goal

**ID**: FEAT-FP-002
**Source**: Plan Feature agent (self-contained â€” no plan file)

Make deterministic Briefs read like they were written by a human editor, not scraped by a machine. FEAT-FP-001 fixed _what_ evidence gets selected; this feature fixes _how it reads_. After this feature, a Brief contains no heading fragments glued to sentences, no raw newlines inside bullets, no bullets that open with an unresolved "This led toâ€¦", no boilerplate ("Last Updated: May 2026â€¦"), no stat repeated three times in slightly different words, and no comparison table of context-free percentages. Findings are organized into topic groups with nested parent-child bullets, and the comparison table says _what_ each figure measures.

Reference failure artifact: the "State of EV car sales in US in 2026" brief (post-FEAT-FP-001 run), which exhibits every target failure mode.

## 2. Technical Context

### Approach

Seven coordinated fixes, all local and deterministic (wink-nlp only â€” no new dependencies):

```text
doc.text
  -> BlockSegmentingAnalyzer (NEW decorator over any TextAnalyzer)
       splits on blank-line runs + heading-shaped lines, so unpunctuated
       headings become standalone segments that die at the finite-verb gate
  -> eligibility: claim text whitespace-collapsed at storage
       + gate 0: boilerplate openers rejected
       + anaphora stitching (antecedent prepended or claim rejected)
  -> merge: numeric-aware near-duplicate collapse (shared %/$ value + 0.5 cosine)
  -> facets: Metric column derived from each value's anchoring sentence
  -> composer: topic-grouped findings (parents + <=2 children), nested sections
  -> renderers (md / html / terminal): nested bullets, per-line newline defense
```

Root causes (all verified in code):

| Symptom                                                               | Root cause                                                                                                                                                                           |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Heading glued onto sentence with raw `\n\n\n` inside a bullet         | Readability `textContent` keeps unpunctuated heading lines; wink SBD splits only on terminal punctuation (`wink-analyzer.ts:169`); claim text stored verbatim (`eligibility.ts:144`) |
| Excess blank lines in `brief.md` sections                             | `sectionBlock` never collapses newlines in `body_md` (`to-markdown.ts:126-130`); key findings do (`inline()`), sections don't                                                        |
| Dangling anaphora ("This led to a sharp dropâ€¦")                     | No gate inspects discourse; such sentences pass all four gates                                                                                                                       |
| Same 28% stat repeated 3+ times                                       | Near-dup merge needs lemma-cosine â‰¥ 0.75 (`evidence-set.ts:55`); different verbs/unit counts push stat paraphrases below it                                                        |
| "Last Updated: May 2026 â€”â€¦" bullets                               | No boilerplate gate                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `Source \| Change` table mixing YoY decline / MoM rise / market share | `pickAnchoredValue` stores only bare `entity.text` (`facet-planner.ts:105-133`); the anchoring sentence is discarded                                                                 |
| Key Findings topically jumbled                                        | Pure salience order interleaves unrelated topics                                                                                                                                     |

Key decisions (all confirmed with the user 2026-07-11):

1. **Block-aware segmentation is a decorator, not an analyzer change.** New `BlockSegmentingAnalyzer implements TextAnalyzer` wraps any inner analyzer (wink or baseline): normalize `\r\nâ†’\n`, hard-split on blank-line runs (`/\n[ \t]*\n+/`), and within a block split after heading-shaped lines (no terminal punctuation `[.!?â€¦:;]` + closing quotes/brackets, â‰¤ 80 chars, â‰¤ 12 words) so `Heading\nParagraph` separates while hard-wrapped prose stays joined. Blocks are analyzed per-inner-call (per-block memoization = cache hits on repeated boilerplate) and stitched into one `DocAnalysis` with globally re-indexed sentences, offset `entities[].sentenceIndex`, and a dispatching `hasFiniteVerb`; the stitched result is memoized per doc text. Both analyzers stay individually behavior-stable for their own suites. Documented limitation: an SEO title glued with _no_ newline before the first sentence is not deterministically separable.
2. **Claim display text is collapsed at storage.** `prepareSentence` stores `text.replace(/\s+/gu, ' ').trim()` â€” fixing all three renderers and the overview blockquote at the source. `normalizeClaimText` remains the dedup key.
3. **Anaphora â†’ stitch with the preceding sentence, else reject** (user-selected over reject-outright and demote). A sentence is anaphoric iff its first word âˆˆ {it, they, he, she}, or âˆˆ {this, these, that, those} with a non-temporal second word (year/month/week/quarter/decade/time are self-contained deixis), or is a bare connective (however, but, meanwhile, still, additionally, also, moreover, furthermore, yet, instead, nevertheless, nonetheless). Antecedent = previous sentence (global index) in the same doc. Reject when: no antecedent, antecedent itself anaphoric (one level only), antecedent fails the gates, or combined collapsed length > 400 chars. Stitched claim = `antecedent + ' ' + sentence` with unioned lemmas/entityKeys/numericValues/evidenceKinds, kind recomputed, position index = antecedent's. **The antecedent is consumed** â€” suppressed as a standalone candidate; only the first anaphoric successor (reading order) may consume it; later ones are rejected. Resolved in a single forward pass per doc, _before_ the cross-doc dedup map.
4. **Numeric-aware near-duplicate merge.** `EvidenceClaim` gains `anchorValues` (normalized **percent + money** values only â€” cardinals excluded to avoid over-merge). Merge when `similarity >= 0.75` **or** (shared anchor value **and** `similarity >= NUMERIC_DUP_FLOOR = 0.5`). Greedy over salience order, first match wins â€” deterministic. "fell 28% to 216,399" / "cratered 28% YoY to 212,600" now merge with unioned citations.
5. **Comparison table gains a derived Metric column** (user-selected over comparability-gate and drop-facet). `pickAnchoredValue` returns `{ value, sentence }`; a pure `deriveMetricLabel` composes `subject + direction + (basis)` from: a priority-ordered subject lexicon over lemmas (saleâ†’"Sales", registrationâ†’"Registrations", shareâ†’"Market share", delivery, price, revenue, growth, demand, production, inventory), a basis regex (YoY / MoM / QoQ / market-share phrasings), and a direction verb lexicon (fell/drop/decline/plunge/crater/down â†’ "decline"; rose/grow/increase/climb/jump/up â†’ "rise"). Example labels: `Sales decline (YoY)`, `Sales rise (MoM)`, `Market share`. Unlabelable rows are dropped; < 2 labeled rows â‡’ no table. Applies to percent facet plans only â€” money `Price` columns stay 2-column (self-describing). `query-profile.ts` is unchanged.
6. **Findings are topic-grouped with nested children** (user-selected over flat-reorder and keep-salience). New pure `groupClaimsByTopic(claims, analyzer, threshold)`: greedy in salience order, a claim joins the first group whose **parent** has `similarity >= TOPIC_THRESHOLD = 0.4` (below the 0.5 merge floor), else founds a group â€” parent is always the group's highest-salience claim. Called from the composer so `EvidenceSet.claims` stays the flat ranked truth and `metadata.evidence` counts are unchanged. **Parents count toward `LENGTH_BUDGETS`**; each finding carries â‰¤ 2 children (`MAX_CHILDREN_PER_FINDING`) from its group; remainder spills to sections, where each parent bullet nests its remaining group members as indented child bullets. `underBudget`/`limited_evidence` keyed to parent count. Composer coverage and section `citations[]` union children citations.
7. **`KeyFinding.children` is an additive schema change; no backwards compatibility** (user-confirmed 2026-07-11: app still in development). New leaf `ChildFinding = { text, citations }` (no editorial/facet/recursion); `KeyFinding.children: z.array(ChildFinding).default([])`; `superRefine` requires every child citation to resolve to a declared source and every child to carry â‰¥ 1 citation. `BRIEF_SCHEMA_VERSION` stays `'0.2'`. All construction sites are swept in one task (typecheck finds them): `llm.ts` `normalizeFindings` (emits `children: []`), `citation-validator.ts` (scans child text; a stripped parent drops its children), test-helpers, protocol/core arbitraries and factories.
8. **Three renderers, not two.** Besides `to-html.ts` and `to-markdown.ts`, the CLI terminal renderer `apps/cli/src/render/brief-terminal.ts` must render children and is snapshot-pinned (`brief-terminal.spec.ts`, `e2e/brief-render.spec.ts`). The HTML inertness contract is preserved (escape-before-parse, internal `#src-n` anchors only, no tags beyond ul/li/sup/a/span for citations).

### Spec-Specific Overrides

- **Synthesis stays pure and log-free** (unchanged FEAT-FP-001 exception to "structured logging everywhere") â€” observability via `metadata.evidence` and notices.
- **No new dependencies** â€” everything builds on `wink-nlp@2.4.0` + `wink-eng-lite-web-model@1.8.1` already in `@yantra/core`.
- No other overrides â€” see memory.
